title: Troubleshooting Siphoned Traps and Vent Blockages
description: When fixture drains gurgle or emit foul odors, a compromised vent system is often the primary suspect. Without proper atmospheric pressure entering the drainage line, flowing water creates a vacuum effect that pulls the protective water seal directly out of the P-trap. Common causes include debris or bird nests at the roof vent stack termination, or incorrectly installed air admittance valves. Troubleshooting requires inspecting the vent terminal, verifying trap arms are properly pitched, and testing atmospheric air intake. Restoring continuous airflow equalizes system pressure, preserving the essential liquid barrier that stops hazardous sewer gases from entering living spaces.

Troubleshooting Siphoned Traps and Vent Blockages

When fixture drains gurgle or emit foul odors, a compromised vent system is often the primary suspect. Without proper atmospheric pressure entering the drainage line, flowing water creates a vacuum effect that pulls the protective water seal directly out of the P-trap. Common causes include debris or bird nests at the roof vent stack termination, or incorrectly installed air admittance valves. Troubleshooting requires inspecting the vent terminal, verifying trap arms are properly pitched, and testing atmospheric air intake. Restoring continuous airflow equalizes system pressure, preserving the essential liquid barrier that stops hazardous sewer gases from entering living spaces.
